# FormatDate

Writes a date as text, following a format pattern.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
FormatDate(date, format)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | string | The date to write: a string in one of the forms `ParseDate` accepts. A string in no accepted form is a runtime error, as is any other type, null included. |
| `format` | string | The pattern, read from left to right. These runs of letters are replaced by a value: `yyyy` the four-digit year; `MM` and `M` the month; `dd` and `d` the day; `HH` and `H` the hour, from 0 to 23; `mm` and `m` the minute; `ss` and `s` the second; `fff` the millisecond, in three digits. The two-letter forms write two digits, with a leading zero; the one-letter forms write no leading zero. A run of `T` or of `Z` is copied as it is. Text between single quotes is copied without its quotes, and two single quotes write one single quote, inside quoted text or outside it. Every character that is not an ASCII letter is copied as it is. Any other run of an ASCII letter, such as `yy`, `ddd` or `h`, and quoted text that is not closed, are a runtime error, as is a format that is not a string, null included. An empty format gives the empty string. |

## Returns

String. The text the pattern gives for date. Never null.

## Remarks

The values written are those of the date in UTC, with ASCII digits, the same on every machine.

## Example

`FormatDate("2024-01-15T09:05:00Z", "dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm")` returns `"15/01/2024 09:05"`.

`FormatDate("2024-01-15", "'Day' d")` returns `"Day 15"`.
